article.title: Can We Continue to Vote Blue No Matter Who?
article.author: Rochester Red Star: News from Rochester DSA
article.content: by Greg B. Many people in Rochester DSA have asked whether the chapter should release a voter guide for the 2026 elections, and we’ve debated it in our Electoral Working Group. Unlike other organizations, DSA’s endorsements are highly selective and usually go to candidates who are members, agree to join, and help grow DSA; members often view a voter guide as a way to guide non-member supporters on our perspective on an election. Others think it’s a waste of time and misleading since people often confuse our “recommendation” for an actual endorsement. After examining the 2026 general election ballot, I’ve decided to recommend the chapter not make a voter guide. The results in Rochester were already decided in the primaries, and most of them weren’t even competitive. No Republican has a realistic chance to win the governorship, attorney general, comptroller, or congressional seat. The question shouldn’t be whether these candidates are better than their Republican opponents; it should be what their records are and what it would take to create conditions for future elections with meaningful stakes. Even though these races are uncompetitive, I will still vote out of an odd sense of obligation or ritual. I’ll still vote for State Senator Samra Brouk and Assemblymember Harry Bronson even though they’re not socialists and don’t currently co-sponsor several pieces of legislation from the Democratic Socialists in Office Committee. They’re progressive on many issues, and I’d like to talk with them when there are things we absolutely need to push for. The only politicians I could not vote for, however, are Governor Kathy Hochul, Comptroller Tom DiNapoli, and Congressman Joe Morelle. Kathy Hochul – Governor Kathy Hochul stepped into the governorship after Andrew Cuomo was chased out by scandal, and has largely operated in a similar manner, as a defender of the rich, the well-connected, and specifically, the fossil fuel industry. Governor Cuomo was the biggest obstacle to progressive legislation, but when Democrats overcame Republican majorities and the Independent Democratic Conference, Cuomo gave in, signing multiple pieces of progressive legislation he previously opposed while claiming credit for their passage. Similarly, the NY Senate and Assembly recently passed a Data Center moratorium bill that would have stopped the construction of environmentally destructive data centers, but Hochul refused to sign it, instead issued a weakened Data Center Moratorium executive order , and has received national credit for doing so. Hochul’s issues are wide and far-reaching, but her rollbacks of climate action this year have been particularly destructive. It’s also been personally infuriating to me as someone who previously worked on NY state climate issues in 2022-2023. To start, Hochul rolled back the All-Electric Buildings Act, which she signed in 2023, that requires new buildings to use electric heat instead of gas. Her administration previously spent two years defending it in court, and told a judge that delaying it would cause New Yorkers irreparable harm. A month later, she agreed to delay it anyway. She also shelved the carbon pricing program she had promised, and after talks with Trump, she approved an underwater gas pipeline that state regulators had previously rejected. Also, in this year’s budget, she pushed through changes to the state’s landmark climate law, the CLCPA, including changes to how emissions are counted so methane appears less harmful on paper as a handout to climate polluters. It doesn’t matter if Hochul is doing this as a favor to the fossil fuel industry or because she’s under pressure from Trump. She has followed the Cuomo model of defending the rich and powerful, and posing as a progressive when she’s forced to give in to pressure from the left. Tom DiNapoli – Comptroller I imagine most of us don’t know what a comptroller is, but Tom DiNapoli wields enormous power as the sole trustee of the NY State Common Retirement Fund worth billions of dollars. With that power, DiNapoli has purchased over $100 million more worth of Israeli bonds since October 7th. The state owns over $340 million in Israeli bonds. That’s more than the NY State Common Retirement Fund holds in all other foreign government bonds combined. This is extremely odd considering Israeli bonds are not the most reliable or high-return investments. To be clear, the main issue is not how good or bad of an investment these are, but the fact that it’s helping support a state that has committed genocide according to the UN , Human Rights Watch , Amnesty International , and many other human rights organizations. DiNapoli’s insistence on purchasing and holding Israeli bonds is only one issue. According to his primary challengers, the state fund also owns $430 million worth of Palantir stock, a company that serves ICE and the military-industrial complex in more efficiently kidnapping and assaulting our neighbors, and killing families overseas. DiNapoli says the stocks are held passively through index funds, but he said he will make no effort to divest from them. DiNapoli is little talked about, but tremendously powerful and has used his position to protect Israel and US imperial interests. Joe Morelle – Congressman Joe Morelle is seeking his fifth term after easily defeating progressive candidate Robin Wilt in June’s primary, her third challenge against him. Like Hochul and DiNapoli, Morelle will criticize Trump and espouse progressive values, but he is far more conservative than this district’s politics. On January 22, 2025, he was one of 46 House Democrats who voted with Republicans to pass the Laken Riley Act, which empowered ICE to kidnap and detain people with no conviction required. He opposes the construction of a federal ICE facility in Rochester’s federal building, which is odd, since he voted to allow masked ICE agents to take people off our streets. He was also a cheerleader for Israel’s genocide, refusing to cosponsor a simple humanitarian aid resolution for Gaza, and refusing to sign a letter saying he opposed Israel’s use of starvation tactics. On July 15th, 2026, after there was no more denying what Israel had done, 104 Congress members voted for the Massie Amendment, which would have eliminated $3.3 billion in aid to Israel. Joe Morelle was one of the 98 Democrats who wanted to continue giving military aid to Israel, despite the pleas of his constituents. How Should We Vote ROC DSA will likely not make a voter guide for the 2026 general election. If you asked me who you should vote for, these politicians or their Republican opponents, I’d say we’re asking the wrong question. It doesn’t matter if you vote for them or withhold it. They’ve already won. The political reality is that they had the election locked down before the primary. I’m not saying to despair, and I’m not saying you shouldn’t vote. Instead, I am saying we need to do more. The stakes are so high. The climate crisis is deadly and will accelerate at an alarming rate in our lifetime. Israel will never stop until it is forced to stop. Instead of waiting for elections and weighing our options, we need to act now. We are too weak to defeat Joe Morelle, who raised over $1,580,000 for his re-election and had a Silicon Valley billionaire-funded Super PAC spend $624,734 on his behalf. Instead, we need to develop a serious strategy, organize now, with what we have, and build victory upon victory so we can win real power that will stop Israel’s actions and build a sustainable energy future, with public healthcare for all, a good jobs guarantee, housing for all, and more.
